rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a promising baseline. config_017 uses scgpt (a strong RNA encoder) and imagenet_vit_l (a powerful image encoder) with weighted fusion, which balances complexity and potential performance. This configuration clarifies the effectiveness of combining advanced encoders with weighted fusion for multimodal singleprofile data, providing foundational insights without overfitting to specific design choices.

The existing evidence shows that using weighted fusion with scgpt and imagenet_vit_l achieves 0.422 accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method to concat (while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation unchanged) improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation of the current setup with exploration of a key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that config_002 (scgpt RNA, ImageNet ViT-L image encoder, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.4348). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 while keeping other parameters identical to config_002. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance, a critical design decision. It balances exploration (testing a new RNA encoder) with exploitation (building on the successful concat fusion and ImageNet ViT-L image encoder from config_002).

The existing evidence shows config_023 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.535). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 and using weighted fusion instead of concat, which could improve performance by leveraging a simpler image encoder and more effective fusion. It balances exploitation (similar RNA encoder) and exploration (different image encoder/fusion), addressing uncertainty about image encoder choices while building on the strong RNA encoder from config_023.

Existing evidence shows config_019 (0.639 accuracy) is the top performer with pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image. This experiment tests scgpt RNA and imagenet_vit_l image, which could reveal if encoder choices significantly impact performance. It clarifies the importance of RNA/image encoders while maintaining similar aggregation/fusion settings, balancing exploitation of top-performing components with exploration of alternative encoders.

The existing evidence shows that config_019 (pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.638). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation while keeping pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image encoders, which are key components of the current best configuration. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation could further improve performance, balancing exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a novel aggregation method.

The existing evidence shows config_019 (0.639 accuracy) is the best so far using pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could reveal if these changes improve performance. It balances exploitation (building on successful components) and exploration (testing alternative fusion/aggregation strategies).

The existing evidence shows config_019 (0.639 accuracy) is the best so far using pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests scgpt RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. It clarifies whether switching aggregation (transformer vs avgpool) and fusion (concat vs weighted) could improve performance. This balances exploration of key design choices (aggregation/fusion) while leveraging the high-performing resnet50 image encoder from config_019.

The existing evidence shows config_019 (multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted) has the highest accuracy (0.639). The next experiment should test a similar setup but with transformer aggregation (config_050) to explore if this improves performance. This balances exploitation of the current best configuration and exploration of aggregation methods, which are critical for multimodal fusion.

The existing evidence shows config_019 (0.639 accuracy) is the best so far, but uncertainty remains about whether transformer aggregation or different RNA encoders could improve performance further. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation, which could potentially outperform config_019's pca_n2000 and avgpool setup. It directly addresses the critical design choice of aggregation method while maintaining high-performing components like resnet50 and weighted fusion.
